kicker: RSI-Anything, world models in the loop

scenes.headline: How RSI-Anything puts a world model in the loop
scenes.sub: Predict first, pay for feedback second, keep only what works as a pair.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Loopy! This paper puts a world model inside a self-improvement loop. Here is how that loop works.

scenes.text: Predict each candidate's outcome, spend real feedback on the best one, and keep an update only if policy and world model work as a pair.
scenes.say: The idea: predict each candidate's outcome, pay for real feedback only on the best one, and keep an update only if policy and world model still work as a pair.

steps.say: The policy proposes a few candidates. The world model predicts what each one would do.
Only the best predicted candidate is executed, so costly feedback goes where it should pay off.
The outcome is stored beside its prediction. It trains the policy, and retrains the world model if predictions have drifted.
Then the gate: the new pair must beat the old pair, or both roll back.

left.title: Update each part alone
items: World model is wrong exactly there
left.say: Update the parts separately and they can break each other: a new policy proposes actions the old world model never saw.

right.title: Gate the assembled pair
items: Compare new pair with old pair
right.say: So the pair is judged as one system.

steps.say: In the paper's figure, the top band is one round of interaction.
Below it, the checks that decide which pair carries forward.

steps.label: old and new, crossed
steps.say: The GUI experiment tests every pairing of old and new policy with old and new world model.

steps.label: reported controller
steps.note: the world model is never consulted
steps.say: Under the reported controller only the policy row matters. The gate had switched the world model off.

steps.label: world-model ranking
steps.note: the updated world model does the work
steps.say: Rank actions with the world model instead, and the updated world column wins.

scenes.title: Code repair, coder held fixed
scenes.say: In code repair, the world model ranks a frozen coder's patches. Better ranking lifts hidden-test success, and retraining it adds a little more.

scenes.text: A world model earns its place by choosing what gets real feedback. Crossed tests show it did.
scenes.say: The lesson: a world model earns its place by choosing what gets real feedback. Crossed tests show whether it did.

recap: Predict, then pay for one real outcome
Gate the policy and world model as a pair
Crossed tests show which part earned it
scenes.say: Predict, then pay for one outcome. Gate the pair. And test it crossed.
